provenance.planning_scope: Current first package only: vowelled MSA foundational sequence with named country spoken narration, plus country-specific crisis catch-up literacy/science/health/WASH. Count only children whose spoken layer and entry route are actually supplied; later MSA professional/research editions are excluded.
provenance.population_ceiling_context: 30M out-of-school ages 5–18 across 12 countries is a contextual cohort, not an Arabic-speaking or reachable-reader denominator. It is not added to in-school learning-poverty cohorts. The 400M/467M speech headlines do not enter R.

R.basis: Base R2 is a direct joint judgment of hundreds-of-thousands newly comfortable Urdu users across the two localized first-year/methods packages, not an arithmetic consequence of two R2 labels. Each component could occupy different parts of its broad band; together they may cross 1m, so favorable R3 is explicit. The cautious joint endpoint R2 is consistent with Pakistan's own cautious R2 component. Hindi's much larger population and professional reach are excluded completely from this residual score.

Combining that with the exact stage discontinuity supports a 100k–10M planning interval, with the stated baseline; legacy whole-OpenLogic R4 is not copied onto this first package.

population_ceiling_context.semantics: Subtraction of matched census-language categories; not exact same-name L1 components. Non-reporting does not prove no competence, and reported bilingualism does not prove academic comfort. No census fraction is multiplied into a current educational cohort.

provenance.thresholds: R2 requires at least 100k jointly eligible residual learners; R3 requires at least 1M. One million is 1.49% of the aged no-reported-bridge context; that is a threshold, not an estimated share. National STEM enrollment is only 9.85M across all languages/levels, so a first-year-only R4 would need a separately evidenced noninstitutional/multicohort audience.

R.basis: The aged census language category minus reported English-or-Hindi subsidiary-language union establishes a large no-reported-bridge context, not an academically ready or newly served count. Combining that with the exact stage discontinuity supports a 100k–10M planning interval, with the stated baseline; legacy whole-OpenLogic R4 is not copied onto this first package.

provenance.calibration_type: source-informed provisional planning judgment, not a confidence interval or observed effect
provenance.planning_scope: Current Tamil-English first-year STEM/computing/management bridge with worked problems, offline simulations and introductory research methods. Later professional education and all school grades are outside this R.

population_ceiling_context.semantics: Subtraction of matched census-language categories; not exact same-name L1 components. Non-reporting does not prove no competence, and reported bilingualism does not prove academic comfort. No census fraction is multiplied into a current educational cohort.

provenance.thresholds: R2 requires at least 100k jointly eligible residual learners; R3 requires at least 1M. One million is 1.82% of the aged no-reported-bridge context; that is a threshold, not an estimated share. National STEM enrollment is only 9.85M across all languages/levels, so a first-year-only R4 would need a separately evidenced noninstitutional/multicohort audience.

scenarios.baseline: R2 for the current package's joint residual, a provisional judgment.
scenarios.favorable: R3; R4 requires a separately defined and costed broader curriculum, not inflation of this package.

One million is 2.17% of the aged no-reported-bridge context; that is a threshold, not an estimated share. National STEM enrollment is only 9.85M across all languages/levels, so a first-year-only R4 would need a separately evidenced noninstitutional/multicohort audience.

scenarios.cautious: R2 after crediting existing books, bilingual capacity and stage prerequisites.
scenarios.baseline: R3 for the current package's joint residual, a provisional judgment.
scenarios.favorable: R3; R4 requires a separately defined and costed broader curriculum, not inflation of this package.

provenance.base_basis: The aged census language category minus reported English-or-Hindi subsidiary-language union establishes a large no-reported-bridge context, not an academically ready or newly served count. Combining that with the exact stage discontinuity supports a 100k–10M planning interval, with the stated baseline; legacy whole-OpenLogic R4 is not copied onto this first package.

provenance.population_ceiling_context: 51.9M employed people in 2024, including 17.4M industry/construction workers, are nested—not additive. They are territorial workforce observations, not exact Vietnamese reading counts. 89M speech estimate is older and broader.
provenance.thresholds: A 1M residual among 17.4M industry/construction workers requires 5.75% to jointly need this curriculum, use Vietnamese more comfortably than existing routes, and lack an equivalent accessible package. No 5.75% eligibility rate is asserted. A >10M residual cannot be inferred from the current evidence.

R.basis: Official secondary entry-grade registrations are already million-scale, and the package spans six grades plus ALS/TVET. Combined with offline-access gaps and the explicit bilingual design this supports a provisional R3, not proof all secondary learners lack resources.

provenance.calibration_type: source-informed provisional planning judgment, not a confidence interval or observed effect
provenance.planning_scope: Current 120 Filipino-English STEM-Kabuhayan micro-lessons for grades 7–12, ALS and TVET, with replaceable home-language tracks, worked answers and offline distribution. Not the whole Philippine population or later research spine.
provenance.population_ceiling_context: 109,035,343 residents in 2020 is not Filipino readership. The aged 2,011,190 grade 7 + grade 11 early registrations contextualize educational scale only; no national-to-Filipino conversion is performed.
provenance.thresholds: R2 requires >=100k distinct learners with a material content/language/format improvement; R3 requires >=1M. The threshold must exclude learners already adequately served by DepEd/TESDA/UPOU/STARBOOKS and those who require a home-language track not yet supplied.

scenarios.cautious: R2 for residual ALS/offline users after strong existing systems receive credit.

Hindi-medium schooling does not establish comfortable academic comprehension, but nor can its overlap be treated as zero. Audio and explicit transfer reduce the written-literacy barrier. A low-million standing opportunity is a defensible provisional base; the wide range reflects unmeasured Hindi comfort, age/stage match and oral-to-written uptake.

R5 would require almost the entire 2011 mother-tongue count before age, literacy and Hindi overlap; it is not assigned.

R.basis: The current package targets only two grade/country routes, so whole-family 200M speech estimates and legacy Tanzanian R4 are irrelevant to its first-output audience. A hundred-thousand-to-million-scale opportunity is plausible across these large systems but an exact language-by-grade-by-supply joint denominator is absent.

provenance.calibration_type: source-informed provisional planning judgment, not a confidence interval or observed effect
provenance.planning_scope: Current first package only: DRC grades 1–3 Kiswahili completion/adaptation with French bridge and regional-variety overlays; Uganda P4 Kiswahili-L2 support with offline audio. Tanzania/Kenya secondary or advanced editions are follow-on, not counted here.
provenance.population_ceiling_context: 200M global users and 61.74M/47.56M/45.91M country totals are not compatible grade-specific reader denominators and are not summed.
provenance.thresholds: R2 requires >=100k distinct grade-appropriate learners with usable local-language/entry support and a residual gap. R3 requires >=1M such learners. Existing textbooks must be excluded only where they already supply the proposed usable package, not just because a catalog entry exists.
